summary: Technology led the declines on 29 Oct: Alphabet fell 12.6% and Amazon 4.3% after results, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 1.4% and the S&P 500 0.3%. Asian chip stocks split, with SK hynix up 2.6% after record quarterly profit and Samsung Electronics down 4.1%, and the Bank of Japan held at 1.25% on 30 Oct in an 8-1 vote. In resources, Brent closed at $110.80 and WTI at $102.00, European gas (TTF) was up 8.8% on the week near EUR 98/MWh with storage low, and gold and copper eased about 1%. Emerging-market moves were uneven: Brazil's EWZ is down 20.8% over the week and Petrobras 14.5%, while the ECB held at 2.65% on 29 Oct and the dollar was little changed against the yen.

headlines.story: BOJ holds at 1.25% with one dissent and speeds up ETF sales
headlines.summary: The Bank of Japan kept its policy rate at 1.25% in an 8-1 vote (Hajime Takata wanted 1.5%), said underlying inflation has roughly reached 2%, and will raise its annual ETF sales pace to 860 billion yen from January.

headlines.framing: The Japan Times stresses the hold amid rising inflation; Tradingpedia the hawkish signal and yen gain; Le Private Banker the dissent and faster ETF sales.

overlap.reason: Yen strengthened to about 157.3 per dollar after the decision.

indicators.name: US working gas in storage (EIA)

indicators.name: Refined copper market balance, year to date (ICSG)
indicators.note: Positive is surplus, negative is deficit, cumulative within the year. Reached through press reports quoting ICSG.

indicators.name: US reactors at 0% power (NRC daily report)
indicators.note: Count of units shown at 0% on the Friday daily report at nrc.gov (URL pattern .../reactor-status/2026/YYYYMMDDps.html). Autumn refuelling pushes the count up. Counted from the page text, so check the count against the page.

indicators.name: Uranium spot price, month-end (Cameco)

spreads.name: Brent minus WTI

spreads.name: Copper to aluminum price ratio
spreads.note: Copper in USD per tonne (pounds converted) divided by aluminum in USD per tonne.

spreads.name: Copper to gold ratio
spreads.note: Copper USD per pound divided by gold USD per ounce, times 1000. A familiar growth-versus-safety gauge.
